clue.text: Act poorly in hospital, initially in care of charming doctor

indicators.note: the word in tells us the overacting goes inside the word for hospital

parts.note: a san (sanatorium) is a hospital for convalescents
to ham is to act badly, overplaying the part

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A doctor who works charms is accused of bad acting while on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming doctor' is a witch doctor who works charms, and 'of' makes the definition adjectival. A SAN, short for sanatorium, is the crossword hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a witch doctor who works charms and spells, and the adjective describes things belonging to one.

clue.text: Family following direction from top left training class

parts.note: south-east is the direction leading from the top left corner
PT, physical training, is a gym class

explanation.surface: A family follows a route from the top left corner to a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the direction you head from a top-left corner towards the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a clan or branch of a family, especially in Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Sandy area in which to set a TV transmitter once

parts.note: Sandy is a pet form of the name Alexandra

indicators.note: in which to set says the letter goes inside the word for area

parts.note: a place is an area

explanation.surface: A beach where a television mast might be put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which to set' puts A inside PLACE to make PALACE. This north London venue housed the BBC's first television transmitter in 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC began the world's first regular high-definition TV service from a mast at this London building.

clue.text: Bow head, being playful

parts.note: an arch is a bow or curved shape
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours

explanation.surface: Someone bows their head in a mischievous mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a geographical headland, as in place names like Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Archness is coy, mischievous playfulness, so the noun means the state of being playful.

clue.text: Theatre night-lights showing up like neon

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the exposed letters are read from bottom to top
showing means putting on display, so letters inside the words are exposed

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Theatre lights at night glow like neon tubes.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'showing up' wholly to the reversal, leaving the hidden word unsignalled: 'showing' displays TRENI inside 'Theatre night', and 'up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas that is chemically unreactive, the core meaning of inert.

clue.text: Inwardly touching, it may stand in way

annotationWithheld.why: Inwardly touching, it may stand in way (6): TREE (it may stand) inside ST (way) gives STREET, but 'Inwardly touching' then has no clear job and no definition remains; the scan prints the clue this way and no blog parse was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Inwardly touching, it may stand in way

clue.text: Reason suitor's come so far?

definitions.meaning: a suitor calls in order to court, that is, with the aim of going out with someone

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as the purpose of the visit; the second is the everyday phrase for until now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both up until now and, literally, for the purpose of courting someone.

clue.text: In error, so recalculates a higher wage allowance

indicators.note: in error means wrongly, so the letters are put into the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone recalculates a pay rise and gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In error' rearranges SO RECALCULATES A, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator clause in a contract allows pay or prices to rise in line with costs.

clue.text: Insurgents slip first into evacuated towns

indicators.note: into puts the mistake and the ordinal inside the emptied word
evacuated means emptied, leaving only the first and last letters of towns

parts.note: an error is a slip or mistake
1ST, first, written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: Rebels slip into towns that have been emptied of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' written as 1ST gives IST, the figure one read as I. 'slip' looks like a verb of sneaking in but is the noun for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrorists are often insurgents using violence against a government.

clue.text: One approving words by rugby commentator, all being of equal stature

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a commentator might say some try! to praise a score

explanation.surface: An approving rugby pundit thinks all the players are the same height.
explanation.walkthrough: A try is the scoring touchdown in rugby, so a commentator might enthuse 'some try!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometry is equality of measure, so things in isometry are of equal size.

clue.text: Before long, back senior ministers

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
to long for something is to ache for it

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for senior is written in reverse

explanation.surface: An instruction to support the most senior government ministers before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a verb meaning support, but it reverses the abbreviation. 'Before long' is not the idiom for soon but two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachers are ministers of religion who deliver sermons, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Journalist recalled my stage background

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so the journalist is read in reverse

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist
cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A reporter remembers the backdrop of a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns ED into DE. 'my' is the exclamation, a British 'cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the scenery and furnishing of a stage set, the background against which a play is acted.

clue.text: Blades trimmed lad's first beard

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word lad's

parts.note: an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A boy shaves off his first growth of beard with razor blades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blades' is not razors but grass blades, and 'beard' is the botanical bristle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is an expanse of grass kept mown, so its blades are regularly cut short.

clue.text: As well to enlist old lady to cultivate fruit

indicators.note: to enlist is to take in as a recruit, so the word for also takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: too means as well, also
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old lady
to till is to cultivate land

explanation.surface: Someone also signs up their elderly mother to grow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lady' is slang for one's mother. The surface's soldiering 'enlist' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small green husked fruit related to the tomato, used in Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Information on line ultimately helping production

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of line

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Data on a production line eventually helps manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'ultimately' gives E from 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Generation is the act of producing something, as in power generation.

clue.text: Strippers convulsed Sid with ecstasy

indicators.note: convulsed means violently shaken, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Striptease artistes leave a man called Sid shaking with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convulsed' rearranges SID plus ECSTASY. The answer is a rare word coined by H L Mencken.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecdysiast is a striptease performer, a word modelled on ecdysis, the shedding of skin.

clue.text: Room Tate organised for little boy's drawing

indicators.note: organised means arranged in order, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: The Tate gallery arranges a room for a child's picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges ROOM TATE. The Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a cupid, a little winged boy depicted in Renaissance art.

clue.text: Regularly missing letters sent out in case

indicators.note: regularly missing letters means every other letter is dropped from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Letters keep going astray when posted in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping every other letter of 'sent out in' leaves the second, fourth, sixth and eighth.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles, scissors or cosmetics.

clue.text: Fleming's latest Bond girl's captivating viewer

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the other pieces hold that letter inside

parts.note: James Bond is a spy
a lass is a girl

indicators.note: latest asks for the final letter of Fleming's

explanation.surface: Ian Fleming's newest Bond girl is a captivating sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's Bond girl is a red herring: Bond is the spy himself. Ian Fleming created James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small telescope, something one views through.

clue.text: Half of old item in morning paper

parts.note: an item is a couple, and an ex is one half of a former couple
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Half an old article appears in the morning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' is a romantic couple, so an ex is half of an old one; 'paper' is an examination paper, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test set on paper, and a paper is a common word for a single examination.

clue.text: Neat-sounding religious concept

indicators.note: sounding says the phrase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a neat drink is wholly spirit, with nothing added

explanation.surface: A tidy-sounding idea from religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat whisky is undiluted: wholly spirit, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The third person of the Christian Trinity is a central doctrine of the faith.

clue.text: I'm hurt with you fencing (in French)

definitions.text: I'm hurt with you fencing (in French)

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the French word surrounds the cry

parts.note: te is a French word for you, as the bracketed phrase says
ouch is the cry of someone hurt

explanation.surface: A fencer admits being hit, in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is what a fencer says, in French, on being hit; 'fencing' does double duty in the surface as the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The French cry acknowledges a hit in fencing, admitting the opponent has scored.

clue.text: In recession after a time nearly all are billions in debt

indicators.note: nearly means the word all loses its final letter

parts.note: to owe billions is to be in debt by billions, B being billion

explanation.surface: During an economic downturn, after a while nearly everyone owes billions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL. B is the abbreviation for billion, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a low ebb, like a falling tide, means in a depressed or declining state.

clue.text: Anger about second-rate work that's accepted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for anger goes round the grade

parts.note: bile is bitterness or anger
B is a second-class grade

explanation.surface: Fury over a mediocre piece of work that has been approved anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B inside BILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bible is an authoritative book accepted as definitive in its field, like the Christian scriptures.

clue.text: Good Swede loses a game

indicators.note: loses means a letter is taken away from the man's name

parts.note: Olaf is a typical Scandinavian name, as of Swedish kings

explanation.surface: A fine Swedish player is beaten in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes the A from OLAF, leaving OLF. 'Swede' is a man, not the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game played with clubs and balls on a course.

clue.text: Woman's right to German title? Not this one

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's entitlement to a German honour is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition teases: the German title for a man would never be a woman's.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German form of address for a man, equivalent to Mister, so not for a woman.

clue.text: One nearly sacrificed savings account, then another

parts.note: an ISA is a British tax-free savings account
another account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: Someone almost gave up a savings account, and then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA (Individual Savings Account) is a tax-free British savings product; 'another' means another account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abraham was about to sacrifice his son on the altar until an angel stopped him.

clue.text: Guide to fingering a brutal criminal in note

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the musical note

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent criminal is mentioned in a note on how to finger someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges A BRUTAL into ABLATUR. Tablature is used for guitar and lute music.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablature is a form of musical notation showing a player where to put the fingers rather than the notes.

clue.text: Obligatory joint —- managed to take from mouth

indicators.note: taken from the mouth means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a knee is a joint and managed means did, giving knee did

explanation.surface: A compulsory cannabis joint was taken out of someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' is the knee, not a cannabis cigarette; spoken, KNEE DID sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed is required or necessary, as an obligatory thing is.

clue.text: Ties, say, bishops and others to pledge

parts.note: bishops, knights and rooks are chess men
to swear is to pledge or vow

explanation.surface: Clergy and others vow to keep the peace by drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishops' are chess pieces, not clergy; 'Ties' are neckties, not draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Neckties are an example of clothing for men, hence the 'say'.
